- If sentiment is negative or neutral in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or shift downward by 1–2%.
- If model shows upward trend after a recent dip or spike, it often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high or adjust to mean of last 5–7 days.
- When sentiment is mildly positive (e.g., 0.20), model may be too optimistic; apply slight downward bias (e.g., -0.5 to -1.5%) to avoid overcorrection.
- If true outcome shows sharp downward correction after a forecast peak, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with 30-day moving average or 10-day SMA.
- For horizon > 14 days, model tends to underestimate volatility; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast if sentiment is stable or mildly positive.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., -1.00), model often ignores downward momentum; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
